strongest_attack: The strongest attack is the unsupported upgrade from a correct fibrewise, set-theoretic criterion to equality of relative schemes over every base. Nonzero H^0 detects geometric failure points, but it does not identify nilpotents or multiplicities in the determinantal failure locus. With h^0(L) allowed to jump, Proj(π_*L) is also not justified as the required relative linear system without base-change control. The finite étale ordering cover exists over a properly constructed reduced-divisor incidence space, but the proof has not shown that this space is the evaluation-failure scheme claimed by the theorem.
theorem_statement: Let B be any base carrying a smooth family of genus-6 curves with balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl data of splitting type F ≅ O_{P^1}(4) ⊕ O_{P^1}(5), and write γ for the scroll projection. Define W_f := (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^* O_{P^1}(−f))|_C for f ∈ {4,5} as in SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (including the minus sign). For an ordered 6-tuple of distinct points (p_1,…,p_6) on a fibre C with Γ = ∑ p_i, the f=4 CE obstruction space H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_4^∨(Γ)) vanishes identically, while H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ)) is nonzero if and only if O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}. Consequently the evaluation-failure locus Z over B is precisely the finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system |W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}| → B; in particular Z is cut out inside the ordered distinct-point configuration space by the single residual isomorphism condition O(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1} coming from the f_2=5 summand.
